candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The pipe friction factor f_D is a dimensionless quantity characterizing frictional losses in pipe flow. It depends on fluid density (rho), dynamic viscosity (mu), pipe diameter (D), mean flow velocity (U), and wall roughness height (epsilon). Each input's physical dimension is well-known from fluid mechanics and SI base units. The friction factor f_D is dimensionless, so all SI exponents are zero.

variables.physical_definition: Fluid density, mass per unit volume of the fluid.
Dynamic viscosity, fluid's resistance to shear flow.

Mean flow velocity, average fluid velocity in the pipe.
Wall-texture parameter, physical height of roughness elements above the pipe wall.
